title: Why Doubling Your Savings Doesn't Halve the Wait

beats.say: You can invest double the money and still not reach $500,000 in half the time.
beats.visual: Two paper runners stand at a starting line, and a torn-paper finish banner reading $500,000 hangs far ahead.

beats.say: Saver A invests $500 a month, Saver B invests $1,000, both earning 7%.
beats.visual: Two paper jars sit side by side. One gets a single coin dropped in, and the other gets two coins.

beats.say: You'd expect B to arrive in half the time, because that's how effort usually works.
beats.visual: A paper clock splits neatly down the middle, and a question mark flutters above it.

beats.say: But Saver A reaches $500,000 in 27.6 years, slow, steady, and honestly boring.
beats.visual: A long strip of torn calendar pages unrolls across the frame toward a small paper flag.

beats.say: Saver B, with double the money, still needs 19.6 years, nowhere near half.
beats.visual: A second, shorter calendar strip unrolls beside the first and stops well past its halfway mark.

beats.say: Twice the sacrifice, and the finish line barely moves, so what's actually doing the work?
beats.visual: A paper magnifying glass slides over the two calendar strips and searches the gap between them.

beats.say: Time is, because growth earns growth, and that snowball only gets heavy late.
beats.visual: A paper snowball rolls down a hill, staying small at first and then swelling fast near the bottom.

beats.say: Look at $200 a month at 7% for 30 years, you only pay in $72,000.
beats.visual: Paper bills stack up one by one into a modest, even pile on a paper table.

beats.say: But the account grows to $243,994, and most of it is money you never earned yourself.
beats.visual: The modest pile of bills sprouts paper vines that branch into a towering stack of new coins.

beats.say: Even a $10,000 lump sum at 7% for 30 years only becomes $76,123.
beats.visual: A single fat paper envelope grows slowly into a medium stack beside the much taller vine tower.

beats.say: So the small monthly habit, kept for decades, outgrows the big one-time windfall without luck.
beats.visual: Tiny paper coins drip steadily from a faucet and fill a large paper bucket to the brim.

beats.say: The lesson is not to squeeze harder, it's to give your money more years.
beats.visual: A paper hand gently stretches a calendar strip longer instead of squeezing a paper wallet.

beats.say: Today, pick an amount you can keep forever, even small, and automate it now.
beats.visual: A small paper gear clicks into place, and a slow conveyor starts carrying coins into a jar.

caption: Doubling what you save didn't cut the wait in half. Here's what's really doing the heavy lifting. 🧩
description: Two savers aim for $500,000 at 7%. One invests $500 a month and the other invests $1,000. Double the money doesn't mean half the time: 27.6 years vs 19.6 years. Compounding rewards time more than intensity. This is educational content only, not financial advice.
first_comment: What's one amount you could automate and never touch for years? Even small counts. 👇
